newsitem.title: UK: Surging coffee prices lift ICO index to 2-yr peak.
newsitem.headline: Surging coffee prices lift ICO index to 2-yr peak.

text.p: Surging world coffee futures lifted the International Coffee Organization (ICO) composite daily indicator price to its highest in 26 months, latest ICO data showed.
The price stood at 168.99 U.S. cents a lb on May 12, the strongest since 171.82 in March, 1995.
The recent low was 44.05 cents on August, 1992.
The ICO indicator is the average of weighted arabica and robusta prices from major markets. The May 12 average arabica price was 253.06 cents and the robusta price was 84.91 cents.
New York arabica coffee futures have doubled since early 1997 on mounting concerns over tight supplies from Central and South America.

Traders said the market would continue to be underpinned through August ahead of winter in Brazil. Two severe frosts in 1994, one in June and another in July, destroyed some Brazilian crop and sent prices spiralling.
